result:
Parking it. That also drops my earlier question about promoting O2: there's no Track A work to sequence now.

**What parking does (derive-roadmap §5):**

1. **Stage 2 (Closure notices)**, the only unticked stage, becomes one item in `specs/deferred_items.md` under `## lock-closures-roadmap — <date>`. The item has to make sense without the roadmap, because the roadmap is leaving `specs/`.
2. **The roadmap moves** to `specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md`, marked `PARKED (<date>) — 1 of 2 stages complete`.
3. **Nothing else retires with it.** This roadmap came from your own words of 2026-10-14, not from a synthesized spec, so there are no methodology or critique files to move.

**O2–O4 (Track A's Ranked list):** these were never stages, so the parking rule doesn't make them deferred items. They stay in the parked file, and the PARKED line names them so they can be found later. Track A was the funded research, so putting them in the backlog would only leave them to age. If you'd rather have them in the backlog too, tell me and I'll add them.

**Tool calls, in order:**

```
Glob  ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/**/*deferred*        # the Deferred-item schema
Read  <that reference>
Read  specs/deferred_items.md                             # may not exist yet
Bash  date +%F                                            # one date for the section, marker and commit
```

Then I append this item, adjusted to match the schema's exact field names:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — <date>

- [ ] Closure email notices for boat operators
      Boat operators get an email within an hour of any of the canal's 14 locks
      closing. Source: the closure log's live feed, polled every 10 minutes.
      Text-message notices are out of scope. Nothing else picks them up.
      Origin: Stage 2 of the lock-closures roadmap (Track B), parked
      when the canal study's funding ended. Planned for writing-plans,
      because the design was already settled.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll every 10 minutes)
      Done when: a notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and a test
      shows an email reaching every address on the list within an hour
      of a new closure entry.
```

Then I edit the roadmap. Under the header I add:

> **PARKED (<date>) — 1 of 2 stages complete.** The canal study's funding ended. Stage 1 shipped (findings: `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`). Stage 2 is in `specs/deferred_items.md` under `lock-closures-roadmap — <date>`. Ranked-list items O2–O4 were never staged and are not in the backlog. A resume would start from them.

Then I move and commit:

```
Bash  mkdir -p specs/completed
Bash  git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Bash  git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Bash  git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: funding ended, 1 of 2 stages complete"
```

The commit goes on `main`, the current branch. Afterwards I'll report the commit hash and the final text of the deferred item. Nothing gets handed off after a park, so the next step for this work would be the notices item coming up from the backlog.
